summary: SCIM path-escape failure for group names containing '/' prevents delegated-admin role provisioning in private deployment
description:
Issue summary: When Nimbus Health Analytics provisions groups via SCIM, any group whose displayName or externalId contains a forward slash ('/') is not correctly translated into a role binding. Impact: newly provisioned delegated-admin groups fail to gain expected role assignments causing administrators to receive 403s when performing tenant-scoped admin actions. This is occurring only in the customer's private deployment behind their edge proxy.

Context: Customer uses a third-party identity provider which syncs application groups into Redwood via SCIM. Some of their groups follow a path-like naming convention (e.g., 'ops/team-a/beta'). The SCIM request succeeds at the API gateway level but the downstream scim-service returns a 400 and the provisioning client reports 'invalid resource path'.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) In customer private environment, attempt to PATCH /scim/v2/Groups/{id} with payload where group.displayName contains '/'.
2) Observe 200 from edge but downstream scim-service returns 400 in logs and rolebinding not created in role-store.
3) Repeat same request with displayName percent-encoded ('ops%2Fteam-a%2Fbeta') and observe different behavior depending on client and proxy combination.
4) Attempt creating group with no slash and observe normal provisioning and rolebinding creation.
observed_behavior: Provisioning flows that include a '/' in group names result in SCIM handling errors downstream (scim-service log shows 'invalid path token' and request id traced at ingress). The customer's admin users mapped to those groups are not given delegated-admin permissions and receive 403s when calling tenant-admin endpoints. The edge returns 200 to the IdP in some cases while the role-store never contains the expected binding.
expected_behavior: Groups with arbitrary characters (including '/') are accepted via SCIM, safely canonicalized/escaped by the ingress and scim-service, and result in correct rolebindings so delegated-admin users have expected permissions.
logs: [ingress-2026-03-10T14:22:11Z] request_id=7c9f0e path=/scim/v2/Groups/ab12 PATCH status=200 upstream_status=400 upstream_error='invalid path token'
[role-store-2026-03-10T14:22:12Z] info=skipped-create-binding reason='group name normalization mismatch' group='ops/team-a/beta'
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10: Support confirmed customer only sees this in private deployment behind their onprem edge proxy; not reproducible in hosted or dedicated clusters with same payloads.

2026-03-10: Reproduced in staging when fronted by an nginx reverse proxy configured with 'merge_slashes on' and default 'proxy_set_header Host' behavior; removing nginx rewrite allows correct provisioning.

2026-03-11: Hypothesis: ingress or upstream proxy is unescaping percent-encoded slashes before Redwood's scim-service observes the path, causing our internal path parser to treat the name segment as a path token instead of raw content.

2026-03-11: Service-level mitigation tested: toggling our ingress 'allow_encoded_slash' flag in staging permitted encoded names to reach scim-service intact and resulted in successful rolebinding creation (regression test added).

2026-03-12: Customer's provisioning client (Okta SCIM connector) appears to send group.displayName raw (not encoded). Their edge proxy is configured to normalize paths, which double-decodes incoming requests in some cases.
comments: 2026-03-10 15:05 - Samir Gupta (Support): Reached out to Nimbus SRE for a packet capture and nginx config. Asked customer to provide example SCIM payloads and proxy rewrite rules.
2026-03-11 09:42 - Nimbus SRE (via Support): Confirmed proxy has 'merge_slashes on' and custom rewrite rules; provided proxy logs and config excerpt (attached in private).

2026-03-11 13:17 - Marco Silva (SRE): Reproduced issue in staging by inserting an nginx reverse proxy with similar settings. Created a short demo script and linked to PR with test harness (see related_github_prs).

2026-03-12 10:03 - Elena Rios (Product): Noted this is a private-only incompatibility; flagged as potential platform hardening item to accept encoded slashes at ingress by default in private deployments.

2026-03-12 16:48 - Aisha Patel (Support): Sent Nimbus a temporary workaround and steps to configure their proxy to preserve encoded slashes; customer confirmed can apply config change but asked for a permanent Redwood-side fix.
workaround: Customer-applied workaround: configure their edge proxy to preserve percent-encoded slashes (disable path normalization/double-decode) or avoid using '/' in group names. Temporary Redwood mitigation: enable 'allow_encoded_slash' toggle for this customer's ingress which was validated in staging and can be turned on in private control plane.
next_steps:
1) Engineering: implement robust path-decoding isolation in scim-service so inbound JSON fields are never interpreted as URL path segments, even when upstream decodes.
2) SRE: schedule toggle rollout for affected private tenant once code fix is available.
3) Support: coordinate with Nimbus SRE to validate toggle and confirm rolebindings are created in production.
4) Follow-up: add E2E tests covering encoded and raw slash cases and document proxy configuration guidance in Private deployment runbook.
resolution: Mitigation applied via ingress toggle (temporary). Engineering work planned to harden scim-service parsing; awaiting PR review and staged rollout.
